title: Frequent winners where only winners are published
question: In grant rounds and lists that publish winners but not applicants, who wins most often and how much of the total do the ten most frequent winners hold?
finding: Arts Commission grants to organizations, fiscal 2020–2022: 169 awards to 123 organizations, the ten most frequent holding 15.4%; 212 more awards went to 199 individual artists, 13 of whom won twice. The older cultural-equity file (fiscal 2004–2016): 1,341 awards to 320 organizations, top ten 14.8%, led by Asian Pacific Islander Cultural Center (with 1 related name) with 35. Community Challenge Grants (fiscal 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2026): 94 awards to 77 groups, top ten 26.6%. The 2026 Storefront Opportunity Grant list names 38 recipients, each once. Without the applicant lists this shows concentration, not unfairness.
how: Each published award is one win. Winners are counted by name as printed, with spelling variants of the same words merged and organizations that the aliases analysis places in one owner-group counted together (3 rows; the note names every name counted). The share is the winner’s awards over all awards in that program on disk; "top ten" adds the ten most frequent. Individual artists and individual medallion holders are counted, never listed. A winner is listed when it won at least twice.
limits: No program here publishes who applied and lost, so a repeat winner cannot be compared with chance or with its own number of applications: an organization that applies every year and is good at it will top this table honestly, and the low top-ten shares here do not suggest a closed circle. The Arts Commission lists for fiscal 2023 and 2024 could not be obtained and 2025–2026 are not tabulated, so the two arts tables do not join up; the download parsed 116 of 148 awards on the fiscal 2021 page. Medallion counts are holdings on one day, not drawing results. An owner-group can be a fiscal sponsor and the projects it holds money for, or two organizations that report each other as related; counting them together is a choice, and the note gives the names so the reader can undo it. The aliases analysis lists the five most frequent winners of the older arts file by single name, which is why its leader differs from this table’s; this table adds the top-ten shares and the later years.
